bundled_tools.name: browser_control
bundled_tools.description: Controls the web browser: open an address, search, click, type, scroll, read the page, manage tabs, go back and forward. THIS TOOL OPENS THE BROWSER ITSELF. Never call open_app for the browser first - doing both launches it twice, the second copy on a different profile with none of the user's sign-ins. 'Open Chrome and go to YouTube' is ONE call to this tool. Read the status it returns. 'done' means it was confirmed - for an open, the url reported back is the page's OWN address, so if it differs from what was asked for the site redirected and the user should be told. 'unverified' means the address was handed to the system's default browser, which never reports back: say it was opened but not confirmed, never that the page is up. 'failed' means nothing happened.

bundled_tools.name: code_helper
bundled_tools.description: Writes, edits, explains, runs, or builds code files.

bundled_tools.name: computer_control
bundled_tools.description: Direct computer control: type, click, hotkeys, scroll, move mouse, screenshots, find elements on screen, and CLOSE an application. Use action='close_app' with 'app_name' whenever the user asks to close, quit or exit a program - 'close Spotify', 'quit Chrome'. Always name the application in 'app_name'; there is no action that closes 'whatever is in front', because that is usually the assistant. To OPEN an application use the open_app tool instead. Read the status the tool returns: 'done' means it was confirmed, 'unverified' means it was requested and could NOT be confirmed - say so rather than claiming success - and 'ask' means nothing was done and the question must go to the user first.

bundled_tools.name: computer_settings
bundled_tools.description: Controls the computer: volume, brightness, window management, keyboard shortcuts, typing text on screen, closing apps, fullscreen, dark mode, WiFi, restart, shutdown, scrolling, tab management, zoom, screenshots, lock screen, refresh/reload page. Use for ANY single computer control command. restart, shutdown and toggle_wifi put a confirmation on the user's screen and do NOT happen until they press it — never claim they are done. Volume, brightness and dark mode can be reversed with the `undo` tool.

bundled_tools.name: desktop_control
bundled_tools.description: Controls the DESKTOP itself: the wallpaper, and tidying the files on it. Actions: wallpaper (needs 'path') | wallpaper_url (needs 'url') | current_wallpaper | organize (needs 'mode': by_type or by_date) | clean | list | stats. It does ONLY those. For typing, clicking, hotkeys, screenshots or closing an application use computer_control; for opening one use open_app; for reading, moving or deleting files use file_controller. Read the status it returns: 'done' was confirmed, 'unverified' means it was requested and could not be checked - say that rather than claiming success - and 'ask' means nothing happened and the question goes to the user first.

bundled_tools.name: dev_agent
bundled_tools.description: Builds complete multi-file projects from scratch: plans, writes files, installs deps, opens VSCode, runs and fixes errors.

bundled_tools.name: file_controller
bundled_tools.description: Manages files and folders: list, create, delete, move, copy, rename, read, write, find, disk usage.

bundled_tools.name: file_processor
bundled_tools.description: Processes any file that the user has uploaded or dropped onto the interface. Use this when the user refers to an uploaded file and wants an action on it. Supports: images (describe/ocr/resize/compress/convert), PDFs (summarize/extract_text/to_word), Word docs & text files (summarize/fix/reformat/translate), CSV/Excel (analyze/stats/filter/sort/convert), JSON/XML (validate/format/analyze), code files (explain/review/fix/optimize/run/document/test), audio (transcribe/trim/convert/info), video (trim/extract_audio/extract_frame/compress/transcribe/info), archives (list/extract), presentations (summarize/extract_text). ALWAYS call this tool when a file has been uploaded and the user gives a command about it. If the user's command is ambiguous, pick the most logical action for that file type.

bundled_tools.name: flight_finder
bundled_tools.description: Searches Google Flights and speaks the best options.

bundled_tools.name: game_updater
bundled_tools.description: THE ONLY tool for ANY Steam or Epic Games request. Use for: installing, downloading, updating games, listing installed games, checking download status, scheduling updates. ALWAYS call directly for any Steam/Epic/game request. NEVER use browser_control or web_search for Steam/Epic.

bundled_tools.name: open_app
bundled_tools.description: Opens an application on this computer. Use whenever the user asks to open, launch or start any app or program. Put the application's name in 'app_name' exactly as the user said it. This tool answers immediately and confirms the launch in the background: on status=started say only that it is opening, never that it is open. If it does not appear, you will be told separately - relay that plainly rather than claiming success. Never say you opened something without calling this tool. To CLOSE an application use computer_control with action='close_app', not this tool. DO NOT use this tool to reach a WEB PAGE. 'open Chrome and go to YouTube', 'open YouTube', 'search the web' are all browser_control alone - it opens the browser itself. Calling open_app for the browser first and browser_control after it launches the browser TWICE, the second copy on a different profile, which is what puts a 'Who's using Chrome?' picker on the screen. Use this tool only when the user wants the application and nothing in it.

bundled_tools.name: reminder
bundled_tools.description: Sets a timed reminder using Task Scheduler.

bundled_tools.name: send_message
bundled_tools.description: Sends a text message via WhatsApp, Telegram, or another messaging platform. Write 'message_text' in the USER'S OWN LANGUAGE, exactly what they asked to be said. This tool answers immediately and sends in the background. On status=started say only that you are sending it, never that it is sent. The result follows separately: status=done means it was confirmed delivered to the conversation, status=unverified means the keystrokes went out and NOBODY can confirm it arrived - say exactly that - and status=failed means it did not go. Never tell the user a message was sent unless the result said status=done.

bundled_tools.name: video_player
bundled_tools.description: If user wants to open a video on YouTube, he will tell you that specificallyIf user wants to play a video, then he wants to call this featurePlays a VIDEO on the assistant's own display, where the avatar normally is — and stops it, mutes it or unmutes it. Use whenever the user wants to WATCH something on screen: 'play the new Dune trailer', 'play that video', 'play C:/clips/holiday.mp4', 'put that YouTube video on the screen', 'stop the video', 'videoyu kapat', 'turn the sound on', 'sesi aç', 'mute it'. Accepts a local file path, a direct video URL, a YouTube link, or a description to search YouTube for. Video always starts MUTED — only call action='unmute' when the user actually asks to hear it. This returns the moment it is asked, before the picture appears: when it answers 'status=opening', say in one short sentence that you are putting it on the display, and do not wait or call it again. Do NOT use 'youtube_video' for this: that optional plugin opens videos in the web browser and summarises transcripts, it never plays anything on the assistant's display.

bundled_tools.name: weather_report
bundled_tools.description: Gives the weather report to user

bundled_tools.name: web_search
bundled_tools.description: Searches the web. Use for ANY question about current facts, events, prices, or topics — always prefer this over guessing. Modes: 'search' (default), 'news' (latest headlines on a topic), 'research' (deep comprehensive answer), 'price' (product cost lookup), 'compare' (side-by-side comparison of items).

bundled_tools.name: youtube_video
bundled_tools.description: Controls YouTube. Use for: playing videos, summarizing a video's content, getting video info, or showing trending videos.
